answer: Each agent bond could be locked in a public contract for a long, randomly assigned period, with rewards earned only while the bond remains at risk and penalties for provable double claims. This does not prove that one person has only one identity; it makes multiplying identities expensive because every rewarded identity needs separately funded capital that cannot be reused elsewhere. A glacier-sized stake may deter a casual attack, while a wealthy attacker can still pay the cost; the karst and garden are just reminders that geography cannot replace this economic constraint.
